facts: Draft PR #362 advanced from fd34276989856de102fae36f84cb77ec9936ca93 to e96409d7da1a1d5df684f06512f12b771410e49e after adding ADR-0230 for durable gap-repair checkpoint recovery.

ADR-0230 binds checkpoint authority to symbol, timeframe, ordered gap-set digest and schema version; defines bounded repair, ownership, threat/failure cases, rollback/recovery replay and obsolescence triggers.
ADR-0230 explicitly rejects age-only or PID-only orphan-lock breaking and narrows current durability claims because portable containing-directory crash durability is not proven.
Prior green workflow evidence on fd34276989856de102fae36f84cb77ec9936ca93 is superseded for merge purposes; fresh exact-head CI is required on e96409d7da1a1d5df684f06512f12b771410e49e.

Issue #230 remains open and fail-closed because safe orphan-lock recovery, portable directory-entry durability, adversarial crash/path/lock bypass replay and policy/test co-weakening evidence are incomplete.
decisions: Keep PR #362 Draft until all remaining #230 gates align on one fixed head and base remains exact current main.
Do not automatically delete ambiguous orphan locks using age or PID heuristics.
Do not claim cross-filesystem crash durability beyond evidence actually implemented and tested.
lessons: A recovery ADR should narrow claims when filesystem or ownership evidence is incomplete rather than converting green CI into authority.
Orphan-lock recovery requires a provable ownership/liveness contract; ambiguous cleanup is a concurrency safety risk.
Any head mutation supersedes prior exact-head merge evidence and requires fresh gates.
